input: Source a vintage leather armchair for the reading nook

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Budget determines whether to shop at auction houses, antique dealers, secondhand markets, or online platforms, and how much restoration is acceptable.
Knowing what 'vintage' means to the user — a specific era, style, or just an aged look — narrows the search to the right pieces and avoids wasted effort.
Leather colour and finish (e.g. tan, oxblood, dark brown; distressed vs. polished) must complement the existing room decor.
The physical dimensions of the reading nook constrain chair size, and knowing the location (home, office, studio) affects delivery and placement logistics.
Whether the user wants to shop locally, nationally, or online — and whether they need delivery or can collect — shapes which sourcing channels to pursue first.
Knowing who will use the chair (adult, child, multiple people) affects the required size, durability, and ergonomic priorities.
Understanding whether condition is the top priority (pristine, lightly worn, or restorable) clarifies the acceptable quality threshold and whether refurbishment is part of the plan.

gold.taskTitle: Source a vintage leather armchair for reading nook
gold.taskDescription: Find and acquire a vintage leather armchair suited to a reading nook space.

questions.title: What is your total budget for this armchair?
questions.description: Establish the maximum spend, including whether restoration or reupholstery costs are factored in, to determine which sourcing channels and quality tiers are realistic.

questions.title: Which era or style of vintage are you after?
questions.description: Identify whether the user has a specific period in mind — such as mid-century modern, Chesterfield, Art Deco, Victorian — or simply wants an aged, characterful look.

questions.title: What leather colour and finish do you prefer?
questions.description: Determine the preferred colour (tan, oxblood, cognac, dark brown, black) and surface character (distressed, smooth, patinated) to match the room's existing palette.

questions.title: What are the size constraints of the reading nook?
questions.description: Capture the available floor space and ceiling height of the nook so that maximum chair dimensions can be defined before the search begins.

questions.title: Do you want to shop locally, or are you open to online or national sources?
questions.description: Clarify whether the user prefers to inspect the chair in person at local antique shops or markets, or is comfortable purchasing remotely with delivery.

questions.title: Who is the primary person using this chair?
questions.description: Understand the main user's needs — adult, elderly person, or heavy daily use — to set the right ergonomic priorities, seat depth, and durability requirements.

questions.title: What condition level is acceptable to you?
questions.description: Establish whether the chair must be in near-pristine condition, or if lightly worn or restorable pieces are welcome — and whether the user is prepared to invest in professional restoration.
